summary: API Gateway accept-queue imbalance causing single-runtime saturation, GPU preempt OOMs and elevated 5xx for enterprise tenant
description:
Issue summary:
During the late-afternoon customer traffic ramp (around 18:10 UTC), Lexalytics reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for multi-request streaming and chat routes. Investigation shows the API gateway accept/hand-off queue became heavily skewed (connection affinity imbalance) causing a small subset of downstream runtimes to receive a disproportionate number of accepts. Those runtimes experienced repeated GPU preemption events and then OOM-triggered process restarts, producing a correlated 5xx wave across the tenant's endpoints.

Impact:
- Customer: Lexalytics Corp (enterprise).
- Symptom: ~40% increase in 5xx rate on their routes; streaming sessions intermittently reset; increased latency for remaining requests.
- Scope: Tenant-scoped; affected traffic peaked for ~15 minutes but with residual elevated error-rate for ~2 hours.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1, Dedicated pool (reserved capacity for Lexalytics).
- Models commonly hit: redwood/gptx-2.7b (pinned by customer) and open/gpt-medium.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Simulated steady burst of 200 concurrent streaming sessions pinned to tenant routes.
2) API gateway route affinity mapping produced accept skew to 3 runtimes out of 24 in the pool.
3) Those runtimes' accept queues filled; scheduler attempted aggressive preemption to serve higher-priority requests, triggering multiple GPU context resets and then OOMs.
4) Runtimes restarted, upstream returned 502/503, apigw retried some requests producing amplification.

Logs / Observations:
- apigw accept-queue depth metric: runtime-id r-10, r-11, r-12 > 180 while others < 10. (dashboard: grafana/redwood/accept-queue-hotspots)
- runtime logs: repeated NVML preemption messages, followed by OOM and watchdog SIGTERM. (s3://logs/prod/us-east/runtime/r-10/2026-03-12.log)
- apigw 5xx rate for tenant: baseline 0.2% -> peak 12% during event.
- No recent model hot-swap or kernel fallback events recorded for those runtimes.

Initial mitigation applied:
- Support escalated to SRE and moved Lexalytics traffic to a warm spare pool (route weight shift) at 18:28 UTC, which reduced accept skew within 2 minutes and dropped 5xx back to ~0.8%.
- Added a short-term per-connection accept cap on apigw route to prevent single-runtime saturation.

Next steps / asks:
- Engineering: investigate cause of affinity imbalance in apigw hashing logic and why ephemeral route weights routed so much traffic to a small subset of runtimes.
- Runtime team: postmortem on why scheduler preemptions escalated to GPU OOMs rather than throttling or graceful degradation.
- Product/Support: validate Lexalytics' pinned model version and whether their request distribution (many long-lived streaming sessions) should be isolated with dedicated streaming runtimes.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: apigw affinity hashing combined with recent route weight change produced high collision probability for certain session IDs. (see grafana/accept-hash-collision)

Hypothesis B: Scheduler preemption policy uses a CPU-centric metric; when accept-queue backlog grows it still attempts aggressive preempt which triggers GPU context swaps instead of shedding low-priority batches.
Evidence collected: nvml logs, runtime watchdog traces, grafana panels (accept-queue, runtime-preempt-count, gpu-reset-rate).
Staging reproduction steps: TTL-lapse + 1k short-lived session churn reproduces skew in 60s (runbook: repro/accept-skew.md).
resolution: Mitigation in place: traffic moved to warm spare pool and apigw per-connection accept cap deployed to prevent single-runtime saturation. Engineering PR to adjust apigw spread algorithm and add circuit-breaker on accept-queue per-runtime merged to staging (PR linked). Permanent fix scheduled in next release window. Customer notified and credit issued for impacted window.
follow_up_actions: ENG-4321: Update apigw hashing/spread algorithm to reduce collision under TTL churn (owner: Apigw team).
ENG-4332: Modify scheduler preempt policy to consider GPU residency and throttle preempt-triggered context swaps (owner: Runtime team).
OPS-210: Add automated alerting rule for accept-queue skew > 50x relative to pool median.
Customer follow-up: schedule a design review with Lexalytics to discuss dedicated streaming runtimes and model pinning implications.
